snapshot.title: Time Jump — 11:00 AM

fields.narration: It is now 11:00 AM on Saturday, October 24, 2026. The cyber incident has escalated to a Level 3 under HUOG-ISP Section 9.3. The Systems & Cybersecurity Lead has confirmed that the threat actor executed ransomware via a scheduled task on GCS-02, encrypting data in the \HUOG-NAS01\projects\cp&l\d3\ and \HUOG-NAS01\projects\cvac\ folders. The NAS snapshot schedule remains disabled. The offline backup OB-1 is three weeks outdated. The off-site backup service’s last good snapshot is from 2026-04-07. The threat vector is confirmed: the attack exploited a cached service account credential (svc-nas-01) on GCS-02, which was mounted to the NAS during the infection window. The team must now decide whether to isolate the Data VLAN and shut down HUOG-PROC01 to prevent further corruption, or to keep it running to manually verify calibration files for D-3 under high risk.
worldState: The cyber incident is now at Level 3 under HUOG-ISP Section 9.3.
The threat actor has executed ransomware on GCS-02 and encrypted data in the CP&L and CVAC project folders.
The NAS snapshot schedule remains disabled.
The offline backup OB-1 is three weeks outdated.
The off-site backup service’s last good snapshot is from 2026-04-07.
The threat vector is confirmed: the attack exploited a cached service account credential (svc-nas-01) on GCS-02, which was mounted to the NAS during the infection window.
The Systems & Cybersecurity Lead has provided a full technical assessment of the threat vector and impact surface.

The Incident Commander must now direct the recovery order per HUOG-ISP Section 9.3: calibration share (verify against the repository hashes) → ops records → the campaign with the nearest deadline → the rest.

snapshot.instructorNote: This is a critical time jump for the recovery phase. The IC must now activate the recovery order from HUOG-ISP Section 9.3. The SL should be prepared to report on the status of the calibration share and the integrity of the ops records.
